answer: One concrete defence is a staking-plus-history rule: every agent must lock a small deposit and complete slow, ferrous-hard proof of useful work before its first trade, so a thousand fake identities cost a thousand deposits and real hardware time. A crystal-clear public ledger records each agent's behaviour, letting peers trust newcomers only gradually. Once an agent reaches the zenith of reputation through consistent honest work, its deposit unlocks — but fraud slashes it instantly, making a sybil swarm far pricier than anything it could steal.
